Rather: ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you﴾ are the dead and the slain, and the later ones are those who will follow them after; ﴿And indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.﴾ 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah said: May God grant you success and reward you with good.

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: Qatadah said: The preceding ones: those who have passed away; and the later ones: those who remain in the loins of men.

- al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Masruq narrated to us, from Ikrimah and Khusayf, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ The two said: Those who died and those who remain.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you﴾ He said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: Adam (ﷺ) and whoever passed away of his offspring. ﴿And We have known the later ones﴾: those who remain in the loins of men.

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ He said: The preceding ones are Adam and those after him, until this verse was revealed; and the later ones: He said: everyone who was of his offspring.

Abu Ja'far said: I think that I said: what has not been created and what is created.

- Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, who said: The preceding ones: what has come out of the loins of men; and the later ones: what has not come out. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.﴾

And others said: By the preceding ones is meant those who have perished, and by the later ones are meant the living who have not perished.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ He meant by the preceding ones: those who died, and by the later ones: those who are alive and have not died.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you﴾: meaning the dead among you; ﴿And We have already known the later ones﴾: their remnant, who are the living. He says: We have known those who died and those who remain.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ He said: The preceding ones among you: those who passed away at the beginning of the nations; and the later ones: those who remain.

And others said: Rather, its meaning is: We have known the preceding ones at the beginning of creation and the later ones at its end.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, regarding this verse ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ He said: the first of creation and its last.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ : whoever preceded at the beginning of creation, and whoever came later at the end of creation.

- al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you﴾ He said: in the rows, and the later ones among you: in the loins of men and the wombs of women.

And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: We have known the preceding ones of the nations, and the later ones of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' informed us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah informed us, saying: Shibl narrated to us – all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿the preceding ones among you﴾: the first generations; and the later ones: the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to me, from Qays, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ He said: The preceding ones: what passed of the nations, and the later ones: the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from Qays, from Mujahid, similarly.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from Mujahid, similarly, but without mentioning Qays.

And others said: Rather, its meaning is: We have known the preceding ones among you in goodness, and those who lag behind from it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ He said: al-Hasan used to say: The preceding ones are in obedience to God, and the later ones are in disobedience to God.

- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from 'Abbad ibn Rashid, from al-Hasan, who said: The preceding ones in goodness, and the later ones: he says: those who lag behind from it.

And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: We have known the preceding ones among you in the rows during prayer, and those who lag behind in it because of women.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from a man who told us from Marwan ibn al-Hakam that he said: Some people used to hang back in the rows because of women. He said: So God revealed ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn Malik informed me, saying: I heard Abu al-Jawza' say regarding the saying of God ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾ He said: The preceding ones among you in the rows during prayer, and the later ones.

- Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi narrated to me, saying: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A woman used to pray behind the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Ibn 'Abbas said: No, by God, I have never seen anyone like her. So some of the Muslims, when they prayed, would move forward, and some would hang back; and when they prostrated, they would look at her from beneath their armpits. So God revealed ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays informed us; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A woman, beautiful and among the most beautiful of people, used to pray behind the Messenger of God (ﷺ). So some people would move forward into the first row so as not to see her, and some would hang back until they were in the last row; and when she bowed, he would look at her from beneath his armpit in the row. So God revealed concerning her ﴿And We have already known the preceding ones among you, and We have known the later ones.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions in my view regarding this is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: We have known the dead among you, O children of Adam, whose death came earlier; and We have known the later ones, those whose death is delayed among the living, and those among you who are newly come into being and have not yet come into existence. This is due to what precedes it of speech, which is His saying ﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors﴾, and what follows it, which is His saying ﴿And indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them﴾, indicating that it is so, since it lies between these two statements, and no speech preceding it indicates otherwise, nor has any come after it. It is permissible that it was revealed concerning those who advanced in the rows because of women and those who hung back for that reason; then, Almighty and Majestic God generalized the meaning intended to all creation, so He, may His praise be exalted, said to them: We have known what has passed of creation and counted them, and what they used to do, and whoever among you is alive, and whoever will come into being after you, O people, and the deeds of all of you, good and evil; We have counted all of that, and We will gather all of them, and We will recompense each according to his deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. This is then a warning and threat to those who hang back in the rows because of women and to everyone who transgresses God's limits and acts without what He has permitted, and a promise to those who advance in the rows for the sake of women and who hasten toward God's love and pleasure in all their actions.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them﴾

By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: And indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, He it is who will gather all the first and the last before Him on the Day of Resurrection, the people of obedience and disobedience among them, and every one of His creation, the preceding among them and the later.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them﴾ He said: i.e., the first and the last.

- al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them﴾ He said: This is from here, and this is from here.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them﴾ He said: And all of them are dead, then their Lord will gather them.

- al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir: ﴿And indeed, your Lord – it is He who will gather them﴾ He said: God will gather them all together on the Day of Resurrection. al-Hasan said: 'Ali said: Dawud said: I heard 'Amir explaining His saying ﴿Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing﴾, saying: Indeed your Lord is Wise in His management of His creation, in giving them life when He gives them life and in causing them to die when He causes them to die, Knowing of their number and their deeds, and of the living among them and the dead, and the preceding among them and the later.

As:

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: All of those, God has known them, meaning the preceding and the later.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 26:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And We created man from clay of sounding (ṣalṣāl) from black mud altered (ḥama’ masnūn)﴾ (26)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We created Adam, who is man, from ṣalṣāl. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta’wil) differed concerning the meaning of ṣalṣāl. Some of them said: It is dry clay that has not been touched by fire; when you strike it, it rings (ṣalla), so you hear a ringing sound (ṣalṣala) from it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Adam was created from ṣalṣāl, from ḥama’ and from ṭīn lāzib. As for lāzib, it is the good (quality); as for ḥama’, it is the mud (ḥama’a); as for ṣalṣāl, it is finely powdered earth. He was named insān (man) only because a covenant was made with him and he forgot it.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We created man from ṣalṣāl﴾, he said: ṣalṣāl is dry earth that produces a ringing sound.

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿from ṣalṣāl, from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: ṣalṣāl is dry clay that produces a ringing sound.

- Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas ﴿from ṣalṣāl﴾, he said: ṣalṣāl is water that falls upon good soil and then recedes from it, so it cracks and becomes like thin pottery (khazaf raqāq).

- Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Man was created from three things: from ṭīn lāzib, and ṣalṣāl, and ḥama’ masnūn. Ṭīn lāzib is sticky good (clay); ṣalṣāl is the finely powdered (clay) from which pottery is made; and masnūn is the clay in which there is ḥam’a (black mud).

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And We created man from ṣalṣāl, from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: It is dry earth that is moistened after it has dried.

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa’, from Muslim, from Mujahid, who said: ṣalṣāl is that which rings, like pottery made of good clay.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: ṣalṣāl is hard clay mixed with sand dunes (kathīb).

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿from ṣalṣāl﴾, he said: dry earth.

Others said: ṣalṣāl means foul-smelling (al-muntin). It appears that they directed this to its being derived from their saying: ṣalla al-laḥm and aṣalla, when meat became putrid. It is said in both dialects: yaf'alu and af'ala.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us; and al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa’, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ṣalṣāl: foul-smelling.

The interpretation of the verse that is more correct is that ṣalṣāl in this place is that which has a sound of ringing (ṣalṣala). This is because God, may He be exalted, described it in another place, saying: ﴿He created man from ṣalṣāl like pottery﴾, so He likened it, may His remembrance be exalted, to pottery in its dryness. If its meaning there were foul-smelling, He would not have likened it to pottery, because pottery is not foul-smelling, so as to be compared to it in stench.

As for His saying ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, ḥama’ is the plural of ḥam’a, which is clay changed to blackness.

* *

As for His saying ﴿masnūn﴾:

It means: altered (al-mutaghayyir).

The scholars of the Arabic language differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿masnūn﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It refers to ḥama’ that is shaped and complete (muṣawwar tāmm). It is reported from the Arabs that they said: sunna ʿala mithāl sunnat al-wajh, meaning its form. He said: It seems that the sunna of a thing derives from this, i.e., its pattern upon which it was placed. He said: It is not from al-āsin (the altered), because that derives from a doubled root sanan.

Another of them said: It is ḥama’ that has been poured. He said: The poured (maṣbūb) is the masnūn, and it derives from their saying: sanantu al-ma’ ʿala al-wajh and other than it, when I poured it.

Some of the people of Kufa used to say: It is the altered. He said: It seems to have been taken from sanantu al-ḥajar ʿala al-ḥajar, that is, when one rubs one against the other. It is said from it: sannahu, asunnuhu, sannan, fa-huwa masnūn. He said: What comes out between them is called sanīn, and it is foul-smelling. He said: From it the whetstone (misann) is named, because iron is sharpened upon it. As for the people of interpretation, they said regarding it something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ubayd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Muslim narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: ḥama’: foul-smelling.

- Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: that which has become foul-smelling.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Umara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: foul-smelling.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: It is moistened dry earth that is foul-smelling, so He made it ṣalṣāl like pottery.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us; and al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us; and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: foul-smelling.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾: ḥama’ masnūn is that which has changed and become foul-smelling.

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: It has become foul-smelling, he said: foul-smelling.

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: from ṭīn lāzib, which is clay that sticks from the dune, which is sand.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾: ḥama’ that is foul-smelling.

Others among them said regarding it: it is moist clay (al-ṭīn al-raṭb).

Mention of those who said that:

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿from ḥama’ masnūn﴾, he said: It means: from moist clay.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 27:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the scorching wind﴾

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the jinn﴾ — we have already explained earlier the meaning of al-jann (the jinn) and why it was called jann. By al-jann here is meant Iblis, the father of the jinn. He, exalted is He, says: And Iblis, We created him before man, from the fire of the scorching wind.

As related:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And the jinn We created before﴾: he is Iblis, who was created before Adam. Adam was created last of creation. The enemy of Allah, Iblis, envied him for the honour Allah had bestowed upon him, and said: "I am of fire, and he is of clay." So the prostration was to Adam, and obedience was to Allah, exalted is He. Then He said, ﴿Get out of it, for you are accursed﴾.

The commentators differed concerning the meaning of ﴿the fire of the scorching wind﴾. Some of them said: it is the scorching wind (samum) that kills.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the scorching wind﴾, he said: it is the samum that kills; a whirlwind struck it, containing fire, and it burned. He said: it is the samum that kills.

* al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Himmani related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Tamimi, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the scorching wind﴾, he said: it is the samum that kills; a whirlwind struck it, containing fire, and it burned. He said: it is the samum that kills.

Others said: it means from the flame of fire.

Those who said this:

* al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the scorching wind﴾, he said: from a flame of the fire of the scorching wind.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Uthman related to us, from Sa'id, saying: Bishr ibn Umarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis was of a living group among the angels called the jinn, who were created from the fire of the scorching wind, from among the angels. He said: And the jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created from a smokeless flame of fire.

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Dawud related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I entered upon Amr ibn al-Asamm to visit him, and he said: Shall I not relate to you a hadith I heard from Abdullah? I heard Abdullah say: "This samum is a part of seventy parts of the samum from which the jinn were emerged." He said: and he recited ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the scorching wind﴾. Some of the people of Arabic grammar used to say: the samum is by night and by day. Others said: the harur is by day and the samum by night; it is said: "Our day became scorching (samma yawmuna yasummu samuman)."

* al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim related to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil related to me, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih, when he was asked about the jinn: what are they, do they eat or drink, do they die, or do they marry? He said: They are kinds. As for the pure jinn, they are wind; they do not eat, drink, die, or reproduce. Among them are kinds that eat, drink, marry and die, and these are those from which come the sa'alin, the ghul, and similar beings.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verses 28–29:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will create a human being from clay from black mud altered [and molded]. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration."﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): [And] mention, O Muhammad, ﴿when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will create a human being from clay from black mud altered. So when I have proportioned him"﴾.

He says: when I have formed him and perfected his form, ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾, so he becomes a living human being, ﴿then fall down to him in prostration﴾, a prostration of greeting and honour, not a prostration of worship.

And Ja'far ibn Makram narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Shabib ibn Bishr narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When God created the angels, He said: "Indeed, I will create a human being from clay. **The commentary on His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said: "My Lord, then respite me until the day they are raised." (36) He said: "Indeed you are among the respited (37) until the day of the appointed time."﴾ (38)**

Exalted is He, says: Iblis said, "My Lord, since You have expelled me from the heavens and cursed me, then respite me until the day You raise Your creation from their graves and gather them to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection." God said to him, "Indeed you are among those whose destruction is delayed until the day of the appointed time, the time of the destruction of all My creation, and that will be when not a single dweller of the children of Adam remains on the earth."

* *

**The commentary on His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said: "My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will certainly make [wrong] attractive to them on the earth and I will certainly lead them all astray (39) except for Your chosen servants among them."﴾ (40)**

Exalted is He, says: Iblis said, "﴿My Lord, because You have led me astray﴾," by Your leading me astray, "﴿I will certainly make [wrong] attractive to them on the earth﴾." It appears that His words "﴿because You have led me astray﴾" are in the form of an oath, as one says "By God" or "By the might of God, I will certainly lead them astray." By His words "﴿I will certainly make [wrong] attractive to them on the earth﴾" he means: I will certainly make Your disobediences appealing to them and make them beloved to them on the earth. "﴿And I will certainly lead them all astray﴾" means: I will certainly misguide them from the path of right guidance. "﴿Except for Your chosen servants among them﴾" means: except for those whom You have purified by Your success and guided, for that is one over whom I have no authority and against whom I have no power.

It has been recited as "﴿Except for Your servants among them, the sincere ones﴾" (al-mukhlisin, with the vowel on the lam, a variant reading, qira'a). Whoever recites it in this way means by it: except for those who have made their obedience sincerely for You, for I have no way over them.

What we have said regarding this is also what the people of ta'wil (interpretation, the explanation of the Qur'an's meaning) have said.

* Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhayr told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿except for Your chosen servants among them﴾: he means the believers.

* Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatada, regarding ﴿except for Your chosen servants among them﴾: Qatada said, "This is an exception (thaniyya) of God, may His remembrance be exalted."

It appears that His words "﴿because You have led me astray﴾" are in the form of an oath, as one says "By God" or "By the might of God, I will certainly lead them astray." By His words "﴿I will certainly make [wrong] attractive to them on the earth﴾" he means: I will certainly make Your disobediences appealing to them and make them beloved to them on the earth. "﴿And I will certainly lead them all astray﴾" means: I will certainly misguide them from the path of right guidance. "﴿Except for Your chosen servants among them﴾" means: except for those whom You have purified by Your success and guided, for that is one over whom I have no authority and against whom I have no power.

It has been recited as "﴿Except for Your servants among them, the sincere ones﴾" (al-mukhlisin, with the vowel on the lam, a variant reading, qira'a). Whoever recites it in this way means by it: except for those who have made their obedience sincerely for You, for I have no way over them.

What we have said regarding this is also what the people of ta'wil (interpretation, the explanation of the Qur'an's meaning) have said.

Those who said that:

* Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhayr told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿except for Your chosen servants among them﴾: he means the believers.

* Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatada, regarding ﴿except for Your chosen servants among them﴾: Qatada said, "This is an exception (thaniyya) of God, may His remembrance be exalted."

**The commentary on His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said: "My Lord, then respite me until the day they are raised." (36) He said: "Indeed you are among the respited (37) until the day of the appointed time."﴾ (38)**

Exalted is He, says: Iblis said, "My Lord, since You have expelled me from the heavens and cursed me, then respite me until the day You raise Your creation from their graves and gather them to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection." God said to him, "Indeed you are among those whose destruction is delayed until the day of the appointed time, the time of the destruction of all My creation, and that will be when not a single dweller of the children of Adam remains on the earth."

The readers differed over His words ﴿قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ (qala hadha sirat ʿalayya mustaqim). The majority of the readers of the Hijaz, Madina, Kufa and Basra recited it as ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ (hadha sirat ʿalayya mustaqim), meaning: this is a path leading to Me, straight.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us. And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa – all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾: He said, "The truth returns to God, and its path is upon Him; it does not turn aside to anything."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Shuja narrated to us, from Khasif, from Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam, and Abdullah ibn Kathir: that they both recited it ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ and said: "ʿalayya" is "ilayya" and has the same meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verses 43–44:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all. It has seven gates; for each gate there is a designated portion of them.﴾

His saying, exalted is He, is addressed to Iblis: "And indeed, Hell is the promised place for those who follow you, all of them." ﴿It has seven gates﴾ means: Hell has seven levels. ﴿For each gate there is a designated portion of them﴾ means: for each level there is a portion from them, that is, from the followers of Iblis, a share and an appointed allotment.

It has been mentioned that the gates of Hell are levels, some above others.

Those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: I heard Abu Harun al-Ghanawi say: I heard Hittan say: I heard Ali while he was giving a sermon say: "The gates of Hell are like this," and Shu'bah placed one of his hands upon the other.

• Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from Hittan ibn Abdullah, who said: Ali said: "Do you know how the gates of the Fire are?" We said: "Yes, like these gates." He said: "No, rather they are like this." Abu Harun described levels, some above others, and Abu Bishr did likewise.

• Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from Hittan ibn Abdullah, from Ali, who said: "Do you know how the gates of the Fire are?" They said: "Like these gates." He said: "No, but like this," and he described them as some above others.

• Harun ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq related to us, from Hubayrah, from Ali, who said: "The gates of Hell are seven, some above others. The first fills up, then the second, then the third, and then they all fill up."

• Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababah related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Hubayrah, from Ali, who said: "The gates of Hell are seven, some above others," and he pointed with his fingers to the first, then the second, then the third, until all are filled.

• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq related to us, from his father, from Hubayrah ibn Maryam, who said: I heard Ali say: "The gates of Hell are some above others. The first is filled, then the one that follows it, until the last."

• Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ali related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti informed us, from Jahdam, who said: I heard Ikrimah say concerning His saying ﴿It has seven gates﴾: "It has seven levels."

• Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying ﴿It has seven gates﴾, who said: "The first is Jahannam, then Laza, then al-Hutamah, then al-Sa'ir, then Saqar, then al-Jahim, then al-Hawiyah. And in al-Jahim is Abu Jahl."

• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate there is a designated portion of them﴾, who said: "They are, by God, abodes according to their deeds."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 45–47:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs (45). "Enter them in peace, secure." (46) And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts — as brothers, on thrones, facing each other.(47)﴾

His saying ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾

He means: We will remove from the breasts of these righteous people whose description has been given any hatred and rancour that some of them held toward others.

The commentators differed about the state in which God removes that from their breasts. Some of them said: That is removed after they have entered Paradise.

Those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya, Abd al-Rahman and Mu'ammal related to us, they said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

And "al-surar" is the plural of "sarir," as "al-judud" is the plural of "jadid," and its plural "sararu" was formed, and the doubled consonant was made explicit in it. The two r's are vowelled because of the lightness of nouns, and they do not do that with verbs because of the heaviness of verbs; rather, they assimilate in the verb so that one of the two letters is quiescent and it is lightened. When something that makes the second letter quiescent enters the verb, they then make the doubling explicit.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 45–47:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs (45). "Enter them in peace, secure." (46) And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts — as brothers, on thrones, facing each other.(47)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, those who fear God by obeying Him and dread Him, avoiding His acts of disobedience, will be in gardens and springs. It will be said to them: ﴿Enter them in peace, secure﴾ from the punishment of God, or from being deprived of a blessing that God has bestowed upon you, and an honour with which He has honoured you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 51–54:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And inform them about the guests of Abraham (51) when they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you." (52) They said, "Fear not. Indeed, we give you good tidings of a learned boy." (53)﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And inform My servants, O Muhammad, about the guests of Abraham, meaning the angels who entered upon Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful (Khalil al-Rahman), when their Lord sent them to the people of Lot to destroy them. ﴿They said, "Peace."﴾ That is, the guests said to Abraham: "Peace." ﴿He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you."﴾ That is, Abraham said: "Indeed, we are frightened of you."

We have already explained the case of the accusative in His saying ﴿Peace (salaman)﴾, and the reason for Abraham's fear of his guests, and the differences of those who differed on it, and we indicated the correct opinion concerning it earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. As for His saying ﴿They said "Peace"﴾, while He means by it the guest, the report about them is in the plural, although they are in a single wording, because the word "guest" (ḍayf) is a noun used for the singular, the dual and the plural, like "wazn" (weight), "qiṭr" (lot/portion) and "ʿadl" (equal), so its report is pluralized, while its wording is singular.

* *

As for His saying ﴿They said, "Fear not."﴾

That is, the guest said to Abraham: ﴿Fear not (lā tawjal)﴾, meaning: do not be afraid. ﴿Indeed, we give you good tidings of a learned boy.﴾

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Do you give me good tidings although old age has touched me? So by what do you give good tidings?" (54)﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Abraham said to the angels who gave him good tidings of a learned boy: ﴿Do you give me good tidings although old age has touched me? So by what do you give good tidings?﴾ That is: by what thing do you give good tidings?

Mujahid used to say concerning this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us. And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿He said, "Do you give me good tidings although old age has touched me? So by what do you give good tidings?"﴾ He said: he was amazed at his old age and the old age of his wife.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. And he said: ﴿Upon that (ʿala anna) old age has touched me﴾, and its meaning: "because old age has touched me" or "that old age has touched me." It is like His saying ﴿It is fitting for me (ḥaqiq ʿala) that I should not say about Allah except the truth﴾, meaning: "that I should not say." And a comparable usage in speech: "I came to you that you give (ataytuka annaka tuʿti), but I did not find you giving."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verses 55–56:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We give you good news in truth, so do not be of those who despair."﴾ ﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?"﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: The guest of Ibrahim said to him: "We give you good news of a certain truth, and knowledge from us that Allah has granted you a knowing boy. So do not be of those who despair of the bounty of Allah, so that they give up hope in Him. Rather, rejoice in what we have given you good news of, and accept the glad tidings."

The reciters differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿min al-qani'in﴾ (of those who despair). The majority of the reciters of the metropolitan cities recited it ﴿min al-qani'in﴾ with an alif. It is reported on the authority of Yahya ibn Wathhab that he used to recite it ﴿al-qanitin﴾ (without alif).

The correct recitation in this matter is that of the reciters of the metropolitan cities, because of the consensus of the authorities upon it, and the anomaly of whatever opposes it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?"﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Ibrahim said to the guests: "Who despairs of the mercy of Allah except the people who have strayed from the path of what is right, and abandoned the straight way by their abandonment of hope in Allah, who does not disappoint one who hopes in Him? Thus they went astray from the religion of Allah."

The reciters differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿wa man yaqnut﴾ (and who despairs). The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it ﴿wa man yaqnut﴾ with a fathah on the nun, except al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i, who read the nun of ﴿yaqnit﴾ with a kasrah. Those who read the nun with a fathah among those we have mentioned recited ﴿min ba'di ma qanatu﴾ (after they had despaired) with a fathah on the qaf and the nun. As for al-A'mash, he recited it: min ba'di ma qaniṭu, with a kasrah on the nun. Al-Kisa'i recited it with a fathah on the nun, and Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' recited both words in the manner of al-Kisa'i's recitation that we have mentioned.

The most correct of the recitations in this matter is the recitation of the one who reads ﴿min ba'di ma qanatu﴾ with a fathah on the nun, and ﴿wa man yaqnit﴾ with a kasrah on the nun, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on its fathah in ﴿min ba'di ma qanatu﴾. Its kasrah in ﴿wa man yaqnit﴾ is preferable, since the consensus is on its fathah in qanata. This is because fa'ala, when the middle letter of the verb is fathah and it is not one of the six throat letters, takes the form yaf'ilu with a kasrah or a dammah in the present tense. As for fathah there, that is not known in the speech of the Arabs.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿We have brought you the truth, and indeed we are truthful. So travel with your family in a part of the night, and follow behind them, and let none of you look back, and go on to where you are commanded.﴾

His mention, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The messengers said to Lot: "We have brought you the certain truth from Allah, and that truth is the punishment with which Allah punished the people of Lot." I have already mentioned their news and their story in Surah Hud and elsewhere, when Allah sent His messengers to punish them with it. Their words, ﴿and indeed we are truthful﴾, mean: we are truthful in what we have told you, O Lot, that Allah is destroying your people. ﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night﴾: His mention, may His remembrance be exalted, tells us, reporting about His messengers, that they said to Lot: "Travel with your family in the remaining part of the night. Follow behind your family, O Lot, whom you are moving with, and be at their rear, and go behind them while they are in front of you. Let none of you turn back to look, and proceed to where Allah commands you."

Similar to what we have said on this matter, the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said.

**Those who said that:**

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Waraqa, all of them together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and let none of you look back﴾: none of them turns back to look, and none pauses.

• al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shababa narrated to us, he said: Waraqa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and let none of you look back﴾: none of them looks behind him.

• al-Mathna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us. And al-Mathna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, from Waraqa, all of them together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

• Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and follow behind them﴾: he said: He was commanded to be behind his family, following their rear at the end of them when they walk.

• Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night﴾: he said: "a part of the night" means some of the night. ﴿And follow behind them﴾: the rear of his family.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verses 66–67:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We made known to him that decree, that the last remnant of these would be cut off by morning.﴾ ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing.﴾

He, exalted is He, says: We made known to Lot that matter, and We revealed to him that the last of your people and the first of them is cut off, uprooted by the morning of their night. The phrase ﴿أَنَّ دَابِرَ﴾ (anna dabira, "that the last remnant") is in the accusative position, as an explanation of the matter of the decree being carried out upon them. It is also permissible that it be in the accusative position by the omission of the preposition, meaning: We made known to him that matter, that the remnant of these is cut off, ﴿مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ (musbihin, "by morning"). It is mentioned that in the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it reads: "And We said that the remnant of these is cut off, by morning." By ﴿مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ is meant: when they reach morning, or at the time they enter morning.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His words ﴿that the remnant of these is cut off by morning﴾: it means the uprooting of their destruction at morning.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And We made known to him that decree﴾: he said, "And We revealed to him."

And His words ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing﴾

He means: the people of the city of Sodom, who are the people of Lot, came, rejoicing when they heard that a guest had come to Lot, rejoicing at the arrival of these guests in their city, hoping to commit the abomination.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing﴾: they rejoiced at the guests of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) Lot, when they arrived, because they wanted to do the evil deed to them.

He, the Exalted, says: We made the uppermost part of their land its lowermost, and We rained upon them stones of *sijjil* [[Probably the original reads (min sijjil), i.e., min tin (of clay), as becomes clear on reflection.]].

As follows:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and We rained upon them stones of sijjil﴾: meaning, of clay.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾:

He says: Indeed, in what We did to the people of Lot, by destroying them and bringing upon them the punishment, are clear signs and indications for those who read signs (*mutafarrisin*), who take heed through the signs of Allah and His lessons regarding the outcomes of the affairs of those who disobey Him and disbelieve in Him. Allah, Exalted is He, by this means only refers to the people of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) from Quraysh. He means: for your people, O Muhammad, in the case of the people of Lot and what punishment of Allah befell them when they denied their messenger and persisted in their error and misguidance, there is a lesson.

The scholars of *ta'wil* have said the same as what we have said concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿for those who discern﴾.

* Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, ﴿for those who discern﴾, he said: for those who look.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababah related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us; and al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us; and Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraydj, from Mujahid, who said: *al-mutawassimin* means *al-mutafarrisin*, and he said: "I discerned in you good, as an extra gift."

* Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Qays, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾, he said: those who read signs.

* al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾, he says: for those who look (*lil-naziri-n*).

* Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, ﴿for those who discern﴾, he said: for those who look.

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding his saying ﴿for those who discern﴾: meaning, for those who take heed.

* Muhammad ibn 'Ummarah related to me, saying: Hasan ibn Malik related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the discernment of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾.

* Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir, client of the Banu Hashim, related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mula'i related to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the like of it.

* Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi related to me, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: al-Furat ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Maymun ibn Mihran related to us, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the discernment of the believer, for the believer looks with the light of Allah."

* Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾: they are those who reflect and take heed, who discern things, reflect upon them and take lessons from them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 76–77:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And indeed, it is on a road that remains﴾ [76] ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers﴾ [77]

Its meaning: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, this city, the city of Sodom, is on a clear road that remains. The one who passes by it sees it, there is no concealment of it, and its place does not vanish, so that a person of understanding would fail to know its matter and the consequence of disobedience to God and disbelief in Him.

And the people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa'; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa'; and Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed, it is on a road that remains﴾, he said: "On a well-marked road."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And indeed, it is on a road that remains﴾, he says: "On a clear road."

67 Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿And indeed, it is on a road that remains﴾: "A road; al-sabil means the road."

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers﴾

Its meaning: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, in what We did to the people of Lot, of what We did to them, there is a clear sign and proof for whoever believes in God, of His vengeance upon the people of disbelief in Him, and of His rescue from His punishment, when it descends upon those of the people of faith in Him among them.

As follows:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, he said: "It is like a man who says to his family: The sign between me and you is that I will send to you my ring, or such-and-such a sign."

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, he said: "Do you not see the man who sends his ring to his family and says: Bring, take her, bring, take her; and when they see it, they know that it is true."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verses 78–79:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, the companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers, so We took retribution from them. And indeed, both of them are on a clear highway.﴾

His words, exalted is His remembrance: The companions of the thicket (al-ghayda) were certainly wrongdoers, meaning they were disbelievers in God. Al-Aykah (the thicket) is the dense, intertwined cluster of trees, as Umayya said:

"Like the cooing of doves over the branches of the thicket, on the drooping boughs..." [The verse is attributed to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi. I did not find it in his diwan, but I found it in Ibn Hisham's Sirah (3:31, al-Halabi edition), from a poem of his lamenting those killed at Badr, which begins: "Will you not weep for the noble ones, the sons of the noble, the praised ones..." Like the cooing of the doves... The verse: al-aykah are intertwined trees, its singular being aykah, and al-jawanih are the perching places. He says: janaha means "he inclined." In Lisan al-Arab (a-y-k): al-Aykah is a thick, intertwined cluster of trees. It is also said to be a thicket that grows sidr (lote trees), arak (toothbrush trees) and similar tender trees, and some specified it as the tamarisk (athl) plants and their gathering.]

Interpreters of the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

- Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to us, saying: Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, who said regarding His words ﴿the companions of the Thicket﴾: "The trees. They would eat juicy fruit in summer and dry fruit in winter."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And indeed, the companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers﴾: "It has been mentioned to us that they were people of a thicket, and most of their trees were the doum palm. Their messenger, as has reached us, was Shu'ayb (ﷺ). He was sent to them and to the people of Madyan; he was sent to two nations, and they were punished with two different punishments. As for the people of Madyan, the Blast seized them. As for the companions of the Thicket, they were people of dense trees. It has been mentioned to us that the heat was sent upon them for seven days, and nothing shaded them from it and nothing protected them from it. So God sent a cloud over them, and they gathered beneath it seeking coolness in it, and God made it a punishment for them: He sent fire upon them, which blazed over them and consumed them. That is the punishment of the Day of the Shade; indeed it was the punishment of a great day."

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The companions of the Aykah are the companions of a thicket."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words ﴿And indeed, the companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers﴾: "They are the people of Shu'ayb." Ibn Abbas said: "The Aykah is a place of thickets and trees in which they dwelt."

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿the companions of the Thicket﴾: "They are the people of Shu'ayb, and the Aykah is the thicket."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Amr ibn Abd Allah, from Qatadah, that he said: "Indeed the companions of the Aykah; and the Aykah is the dense intertwined trees."

* *

And His words ﴿So We took retribution from them. And indeed, both of them are on a clear highway.﴾

His words, exalted is His remembrance: So We took retribution from the wrongdoers among the companions of the Thicket.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 15, verses 80–82:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And the companions of the Rocky Tract (al-Hijr) denied the messengers. And We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them.﴾

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: The people of al-Hijr denied, and they made those who dwelt there and resided in it its companions (ashab), as the Exalted said: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true."﴾ Thus He made them its companions because of their dwelling and residence there. Al-Hijr is the city of Thamud.

Qatada used to say concerning the meaning of al-Hijr, that:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "The companions of al-Hijr": he said, "The companions of the valley."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, while he was mentioning al-Hijr, the dwellings of Thamud, he said: Salim ibn Abd Allah said: Abd Allah ibn Umar said: "We passed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by al-Hijr, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, unless you are weeping, fearing that there may befall you what befell them.' Then he urged (his mount) and hastened until he had passed it."

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Abu Yusuf Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Abi Abbad al-Makki narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Ibn Sabit, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said while at al-Hijr: "These are the people of Salih. Allah destroyed them, except for a man who was in the Sanctuary of Allah, and the sanctuary of Allah protected him from the punishment of Allah." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who was he?" He said: "Abu Righal."

* *

As for His words ﴿And We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them﴾:

He says: We showed them Our proofs and evidences for the truth of what We sent to them with Our messenger Salih, but they turned away from Our signs which We had given them, not taking heed from them nor being admonished by them.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And they used to carve out dwellings from the mountains, secure.﴾ ﴿So the Blast seized them in the morning.﴾ ﴿And what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: The companions of al-Hijr, who are Thamud the people of Salih, ﴿carved out dwellings from the mountains, secure﴾ from the punishment of Allah. It was also said: secure from ruin, that their houses which they carved from the mountains would not be destroyed. And it was said: secure from death.

* *

As for His words ﴿So the Blast seized them in the morning﴾:

He says: The cry of destruction seized them when they awoke on the fourth day from the day they were promised the punishment; and it was said to them: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days."

* *

As for His words ﴿And what they used to earn did not avail them﴾:

He says: The wicked deeds which they used to commit before that did not avert from them the punishment of Allah.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 15, verses 80–82:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And the companions of the Rocky Tract (al-Hijr) denied the messengers. And We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them.﴾

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: The people of al-Hijr denied, and they made those who dwelt there and resided in it its companions (ashab), as the Exalted said: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true."﴾ Thus He made them its companions because of their dwelling and residence there. Al-Hijr is the city of Thamud.

Qatada used to say concerning the meaning of al-Hijr, that:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "The companions of al-Hijr": he said, "The companions of the valley."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, while he was mentioning al-Hijr, the dwellings of Thamud, he said: Salim ibn Abd Allah said: Abd Allah ibn Umar said: "We passed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by al-Hijr, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, unless you are weeping, fearing that there may befall you what befell them.' Then he urged (his mount) and hastened until he had passed it."

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Abu Yusuf Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Abi Abbad al-Makki narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Ibn Sabit, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said while at al-Hijr: "These are the people of Salih. He said: "Abu Righal."

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Indeed, the Hour, which is the hour in which the Resurrection will take place, is coming. Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿So overlook (with) gracious forgiveness﴾, then that was abrogated afterward, and Allah, exalted is His remembrance, commanded him to fight them until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, and He would not accept anything from them other than that.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿So overlook (with) gracious forgiveness﴾, and ﴿So pardon them and say, "Peace," for they will soon know﴾, and ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, and ﴿Say to those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah﴾. He said: All this kind of thing in the Qur'an is what Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to do, until He commanded him to fight, and so all of that was abrogated, when He said ﴿And seize them, besiege them, and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾.

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father told us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So overlook (with) gracious forgiveness﴾, he said: This was before the fighting.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told us, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, regarding His saying ﴿So overlook (with) gracious forgiveness﴾ and His saying ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, he said: This was before jihad was revealed. When he was commanded to fight jihad, he fought them, and he said: "I am the Prophet of mercy and the Prophet of the battle, and I was sent with the harvest and I was not sent with the sowing."
