The interpretation of His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the mighty Qur'an﴾ [15:87]

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, "those versed in interpretation") differed over the meaning of the seven that Allah gave His Prophet (ﷺ) from among the mathani (the oft-repeated). Some of them said: By the seven is meant the first seven surahs of the Qur'an, which are known for their length. Those who held this view differed over the meaning of mathani. Some of them said: "The mathani are these seven, and they were so called because examples, reports and lessons are repeated (thuniya) in them."

Mention of those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The seven are the long ones (al-tuwal)."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, from a man, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The seven are the long ones."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The seven are the long ones."

- Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Walid ibn al-'Ayzar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "They are the seven long ones. None was given them except the Prophet (ﷺ), and Musa was given two of them."

- Ibn Wakie' and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was given seven of the oft-repeated, the long ones, and Musa was given six. When he threw down the tablets, two were lifted up and four remained."

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

- Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "Al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, and al-A'raf." Isra'il said: "He mentioned the seventh but I have forgotten it."

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "They are the long ones: al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and Yunus."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an﴾, he said: "al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and Yunus, in which are the obligations (al-fara'id) and the prescribed limits (al-hudud)."

- Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in a similar manner.

- Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Khawwat, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The seven are the long ones."

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr said: "Inform us from Sa'id ibn Jubayr," who said: "They are the seven long ones." He said: "Mujahid also said: they are the seven long ones." He said: "It is said: they are the mighty Qur'an."

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words ﴿seven of the oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an﴾, he said: "al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and Yunus, in which rulings and obligations are repeated (tuthna)."

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "They are the seven long ones."

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and Yunus." He said: "I said: What are the mathani? He said: In them judgment and narratives are repeated (yuthna)."

- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and Yunus."

- Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The seven are the long ones."

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "They are the seven long ones."

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Qays, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "They are the seven long ones."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah Most High ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an﴾, he said: "Of the Qur'an, the seven long ones, the first seven."

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from Qays, from Mujahid, who said: "They are the seven long ones."

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The seven long ones."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "They are the examples, the reports and the lessons."

- Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Khawwat, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "They are the seven long ones. Musa was given six, and Muhammad (ﷺ) was given seven."

- It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he meant the seven long ones.

Others said: By this is meant seven verses, and they said: They are the verses of the Opening of the Book (Fatihat al-Kitab), because they are seven verses. They also differed over the meaning of the mathani. Some of them said: They were so called mathani because they are repeated (yuthnayna) in every rak'ah of the prayer.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah informed us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, who said: A man among us, called Jabir or Juwaybir, said: "I sought from 'Umar a need during his caliphate. I arrived at Madinah at night, and I was undecided between taking a lodging and going to the mosque. I chose the mosque as my lodging. Toward the end of the night I awoke drowsy, and beside me was a man praying, reciting the Opening of the Book, then glorifying Allah for the length of a surah, then bowing without reciting. I did not recognize him until he raised his voice, and then it was 'Umar. This troubled me, so I went to him in the morning and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, a need with a need.' He said: 'Tell me your need.' I said: 'I arrived at night and was undecided between taking a lodging and going to the mosque, so I chose the mosque. Toward the end of the night I awoke drowsy, and beside me was a man reciting the Opening of the Book, then glorifying Allah for the length of a surah, then bowing without reciting. I did not recognize him until he raised his voice, and then it was you. This is not how we do it in our land.' He said: 'And how do you do it?' He said: 'One of us recites the Opening of the Book, then begins the surah and recites it.' He said: 'What is wrong with them, that they know but do not act? What is wrong with them, that they know but do not act? What is wrong with them, that they know but do not act? And what do they seek beyond the seven mathani? And glorification is the prayer of creation.'"

- Tulayq ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir or Juwaybir, from 'Umar, similarly, except that he said: "He said: He recites the Qur'an as much as he can at times, and glorifies at times. What is wrong with them, that they turn away from the Opening of the Book? And what do they seek beyond the mathani? And glorification is the prayer of creation."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd Khayr, from 'Ali, who said: "The seven mathani: the Opening of the Book."

- Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih and Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd Khayr, from 'Ali, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd Khayr, from 'Ali, the like of it.

- Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us; and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, both from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd Khayr, from 'Ali, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "Ibn Mas'ud was asked about the seven of the mathani. He said: The Opening of the Book."

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The Opening of the Book." He said: "Ibn Sirin said, from Ibn Mas'ud: It is the Opening of the Book."

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Yunus, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The Opening of the Book."

- Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: My father informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding the words of Allah Most High ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾: "It is the Opening of the Book." He recited it to me six times, then said: "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim is the seventh verse." Sa'id said: "Ibn 'Ayyash recited it to me as you recited it to me, then said that the seventh verse is Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Allah has brought it out for you, and He did not bring it out for anyone before you."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, that his father related to him, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said to me: "Begin with Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim," then he recited the Opening of the Book, then said: "Do you know what this is? ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement regarding ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾: "He means: the seven: Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin, and the mighty Qur'an." And it is said: "They are the seven long ones, and they are the hundreds (al-mi'un)."

- Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Opening of the Book."

- 'Imran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Ya'mar and from Abu Fakhitah, regarding this verse ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an﴾, the two of them said: "It is Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book)."

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from one who heard 'Ali say: "Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin, it is the seven mathani."

- Abu al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrate from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he said: "The seven mathani: al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding the words of Allah Most High ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The Opening of the Book, seven verses." I said to al-Rabi': "They say: the seven long ones." He said: "This was revealed, and nothing long was revealed."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "The Opening of the Book." He said: "It is only called the mathani because it is repeated (yuthna bi-ha) each time one recites the Qur'an, one recites it." It was said to Abu al-'Aliyah: "Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim says: they are the seven long ones." He said: "This surah was revealed as seven of the oft-repeated, and nothing long was revealed."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The Opening of the Book."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us; and Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, both from Sufyan, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim, who said: "The Opening of the Book."

- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us; and Ibn Wakie' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us; and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, all from Harun ibn Abi Ibrahim al-Barbari, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: "The seven of the mathani: the Opening of the Book."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu Mulaykah, regarding ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The Opening of the Book." He said: "The mention of the Opening of the Book was made for your Prophet (ﷺ), and it was not mentioned for any prophet before him."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The Opening of the Book."

- Muhammad ibn Abi Khidash narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Harun al-Barbari narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi, regarding the words of Allah Most High ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "It is al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin."

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', who said: "I asked al-Hasan about the words of Allah Most High ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an﴾. He said: 'It is the Opening of the Book.' Then he was asked about it while I was listening, and he recited it: 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin,' until he reached its end, and then he said: 'It is repeated (tuthna) in every recitation.'"

- Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The Opening of the Book."

- Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "The Opening of the Book."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an﴾: "It was mentioned to us that they are the Opening of the Book, and that they are repeated in every recitation."

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: "The Opening of the Book, which is repeated in every obligatory and voluntary prayer rak'ah."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd and Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "My father informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he informed him that he asked Ibn 'Abbas about the seven mathani, and he said: 'Umm al-Qur'an (the Mother of the Qur'an).' Sa'id said: 'Then he recited it, and he recited from it: Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.' My father said: 'Sa'id recited it as Ibn 'Abbas recited it, and he recited in it: Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.' Sa'id said: 'I said to Ibn 'Abbas: Then what are the mathani?' He said: 'They are Umm al-Qur'an, which Allah set apart (istathna-ha) for Muhammad (ﷺ), and He raised it in Umm al-Kitab, and stored it for them until He brought it out for them, and He did not give it to anyone before him.' He said: 'I said to my father: Sa'id informed you that Ibn 'Abbas said to him: Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim is a verse of the Qur'an?' He said: 'Yes.'" Ibn Jurayj said: "'Ata' said: The Opening of the Book, and it is seven with Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, and the mathani is the Qur'an."

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', that he said: "The seven mathani: Umm al-Qur'an."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah al-Utaki narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hanafi, the judge of Marw, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses]﴾, that he said: "The Opening of the Book (Fatihat al-Kitab)."

Others said: "By the seven oft-repeated [verses] is meant the meanings of the Qur'an."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib al-Shahid al-Shahidi narrated to me, saying: Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khasif, from Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam, regarding His words ﴿seven of the oft-repeated [verses]﴾, that he said: "I gave you seven parts: Command, forbid, give good news, warn, strike the parables, count the blessings, and I gave you the news of the Qur'an."

Others, among those who said that by the seven oft-repeated [verses] is meant the Opening of the Book, said: the oft-repeated [verses] is the Great Qur'an.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Imran ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, who said: "The whole Qur'an is oft-repeated."

⁕ Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, who said: "The whole Qur'an is oft-repeated."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Abu Zayd narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, who said: "The Qur'an is oft-repeated." And he counted al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf and Bara'ah.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, and from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: "The whole Qur'an is recited repeatedly."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The mathani (oft-repeated) is what is repeated from the Qur'an. Have you not heard the words of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating (mathani)﴾?"

⁕ I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: "The mathani is the Qur'an, in which Allah mentions one story many times, and this is His words ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating﴾."

The most correct of these interpretations is the view of those who said: By the seven oft-repeated [verses] is meant the seven verses that are the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), because of the authentic report to this effect from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which was narrated to me by Yazid ibn Makhlad ibn Khidash al-Wasiti, who said: Khalid ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Mother of the Qur'an is the seven oft-repeated [verses] which I have been given."

⁕ Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-Ijli narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayc narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ubayy: "I would like to teach you a surah that has not been sent down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan, the like of it." He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I hope that you will not leave this door until you have learned it." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took my hand and spoke to me, and I began to slow my pace, fearing that he would reach the door before the conversation ended. When I drew near, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the surah you promised me?" He said: "What do you recite in the prayer?" I recited to him the Mother of the Qur'an. He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, nothing like it has been sent down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan. It is the seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the Great Qur'an which I have been given."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habbab al-'Akli narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Anas narrated to us, saying: al-'Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, the client of 'Urwah, informed me, from Abu Sa'id, the client of 'Amir ibn Fulan or Ibn Fulan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "When you begin the prayer, with what do you begin?" He said: "Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin," until he finished it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is the seven oft-repeated [verses] and the Great Qur'an which I have been given."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from al-'Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from Ubayy, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not teach you a surah that has not been sent down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan, the like of it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "I hope that you will not leave that door until you have learned it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and I stood with him. He began to speak to me with his hand in my hand, and I began to slow my pace, out of dislike that he would leave before telling me it. When he drew near the door, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the surah you promised me." He said: "How do you recite when you begin the prayer?" I recited the Opening of the Book. He said: "It is it, it is it, and it is the seven oft-repeated [verses] of which Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the Great Qur'an﴾, which I have been given."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl al-Madani, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two rak'ahs in which nothing is recited are like a defective [prayer], incomplete." A man said: "What if I have only the Mother of the Qur'an?" He said: "It is sufficient for you. It is the Mother of the Qur'an, it is the seven oft-repeated [verses]."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The rak'ah in which nothing is recited is defective." I said to Abu Hurayrah: "What if I have only the Mother of the Qur'an?" He said: "It is sufficient for you. It is the Mother of the Book, the Mother of the Qur'an, and the seven oft-repeated [verses]."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from al-'Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah did not send down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan, the like of it," meaning the Mother of the Qur'an. "It is indeed the seven oft-repeated [verses] which Allah, may He be exalted, has given me."

⁕ Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed me, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "It is the Mother of the Qur'an, it is the Opening of the Book, and it is the seven oft-repeated [verses]."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun and Shababah narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed us, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the Opening of the Book, who said: "It is the Opening of the Book, it is the seven oft-repeated [verses], and the Great Qur'an."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Affan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: al-'Ala' narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by Ubayy ibn Ka'b and said: "Would you like me to teach you a surah that has not been sent down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan, the like of it?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "How do you recite in the prayer?" I recited to him the Mother of the Book. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, no surah has been sent down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan, the like of it. It is the seven oft-repeated [verses] and the Great Qur'an."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Habib narrated to us, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, that the Prophet (ﷺ) called him while he was praying, and he prayed, then came to him and he said: "What prevented you from answering me?" He said: "I was praying." He said: "Did Allah not say ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when He calls you to that which gives you life﴾?" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will certainly teach you the greatest surah in the Qur'an." He seemed to forget or [paused], so I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what you said?" He said: "Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin, it is the seven oft-repeated [verses] and the Great Qur'an which I have been given."

Now, if the correct interpretation is what we have said, supported by the reports we cited, then it is necessary that the oft-repeated [verses] refer to the whole Qur'an, so the meaning of the statement is: "And We have certainly given you seven verses of that whose verses repeat one another." If that is so, then al-mathani is the plural of mathnah, and the verses of the Qur'an are described by it, because some of them repeat others, and some follow others with divisions that separate them, so that the end of a verse and the beginning of the one after it is known, as He, may He be exalted, described it, saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating; the skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord﴾. It is also possible that its meaning is as Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said, that the Qur'an was called mathani because its stories and reports were repeated in it time after time. We have already mentioned the view of al-Hasan al-Basri that they were called mathani because they are repeated in every recitation, and the view of Ibn Abbas that they were called mathani because Allah, may He be exalted, set them apart for Muhammad (ﷺ) and withheld them from all other prophets, keeping them for him.

Some of the grammarians claimed that they were called mathani because in them the words al-Rahman al-Rahim appear twice, and that they are repeated in every surah, meaning: Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.

As for the view we have chosen in interpreting this, it is one of the views of Ibn Abbas, and it is the view of Tawus, Mujahid and Abu Malik, which we have mentioned before.

As for His words ﴿and the Great Qur'an﴾, the Qur'an is coordinated with the seven, meaning: "And We have certainly given you seven verses from the Qur'an, and other than that from the rest of the Qur'an."

As related:

⁕ I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and the Great Qur'an﴾: "Meaning: the whole Book."

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do not strain your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them, nor grieve over them, and lower your wing to the believers﴾ (15:88)

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not wish, O Muhammad, for what We have made as enjoyment of this world's adornment for the wealthy among your people, who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, who take their pleasure in it. Indeed, behind them is a severe punishment. ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾, meaning: do not grieve over what they have been given to enjoy, since We have hastened it for them. For you, in the Hereafter, there is what is better than it, along with the honour We have already hastened for you in this world by giving you the seven oft-repeated (verses) and the Great Qur'an. It is said of this usage: "So-and-so strained his eye toward the wealth of so-and-so," meaning that he desired it, wished for it, and wanted it.

It is related from Ibn 'Uyayna that he would interpret this verse in light of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "He is not of us who does not enrich himself with the Qur'an" (i.e., who does not find sufficiency in it). He said: Do you not see that Allah says: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the Great Qur'an. Do not strain your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them﴾? So He commanded him to be self-sufficient through the Qur'an rather than through wealth. He said: And from this is the saying of another: "Whoever has been given the Qur'an, yet sees that someone has been given something better than what he was given, has magnified the small and diminished the great."

What the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said regarding the phrase ﴿pairs﴾ is in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us. And al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Do not strain your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them﴾: "The wealthy, the peers, the equals."

Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿Do not strain your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them﴾: He said: A man was forbidden to wish for the wealth of his companion.

* *

And regarding His words ﴿and lower your wing to the believers﴾:

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Be gentle toward those who have believed in you, followed you, and followed your speech; draw them near to you, do not turn away from them, and do not be harsh with them. He, the Exalted, commands him to be kind to the believers. The two wings of the children of Adam are their two sides, and "the two wings" means the two sides. From this is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And draw your hand to your side (janah)﴾, and it has been said that its meaning is: to your side and your flank.

meaning by "ʿaḍḍā": he took them captive and divided them with his two tongues [[The text of the manuscript reads thus; it may be an error of the author, since the verb ʿaḍḍā, when from taʿḍiya, takes a single subject, and I see no sense in making the subject dual in the author's words.]].

- Qatadah said: Ikrimah used to say: al-ʿaḍh is sorcery in the language of Quraysh; they say of a female sorcerer: "she is al-ʿāḍihah."

- Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿who have made the Qur'an into ʿiḍīn﴾, said: sorcery; the parts of all the books, and the Quraysh divided the Qur'an, saying it is sorcery.

The correct view on this matter is to say: God, exalted is His remembrance, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to inform a people who slandered the Qur'an that he is a warner to them of a punishment that will descend upon them because of their slandering it, like what descended upon the dividers. Their slandering of it was their accusing it falsely, and their saying that it is poetry and sorcery and the like.

We have said that this is the most fitting of the interpretations because of what precedes it from the beginning of the sura and what follows it, namely His saying ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, which confirms what we have said, and that what is meant by His saying ﴿who have made the Qur'an into ʿiḍīn﴾ is the polytheists of his people. Given that, it is known that among the polytheists of his people there was none who believed in part of the Qur'an and disbelieved in part; rather his people regarding his affair were on one of two positions: either believers in all of it, or disbelievers in all of it. Since that is so, the sound meaning of His saying ﴿who have made the Qur'an into ʿiḍīn﴾ is: those who claimed they slandered it, some of them saying it is sorcery, some saying it is poetry, some saying it is soothsaying, and the like of such speech; or who slandered it and divided it by such speech. When this is its meaning, ʿiḍīn may be the plural of ʿiḍah, and it may be the plural of ʿuḍw, because the meaning of taʿḍiyah is division, as the camel and the sheep are divided into parts. And ʿaḍh is slander and false accusation, so the two are close in meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 92–94:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do.﴾ ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists.﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "So by your Lord, O Muhammad, We will surely question these people, who made the Qur'an into 'parts' (ʿidhīn) in this world, in the Hereafter, about what they used to do in this world, regarding what We commanded them and what We sent you to them with of the verses of My Book which I sent down to them, and regarding what We called them to of acknowledging it, and of My Oneness, and of disavowing rivals and idols."

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth, from Bashir, from Anas, regarding His saying ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾, he said: "About the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Layth, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾, he said: "About 'There is no god but Allah'."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Bashir, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾, he said: "About 'There is no god but Allah'."

Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Ukaym, who said: Abdullah said: "By the One besides whom there is no god, not one of you will be left alone with Allah on the Day of Resurrection except as one is left alone with the moon on the night of the full moon. He will say: 'Son of Adam, what deceived you concerning Me? Son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? Son of Adam, how did you answer the messengers?'"

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾, he said: "The servants will all be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about two matters: what they used to worship, and how they answered the messengers."

Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Atiyyah al-'Awfi, from Ibn Umar: ﴿We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾, he said: "About 'There is no god but Allah'."

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾. Then he said: ﴿So on that Day, no person nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾, he said: "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than them; rather He will say to them, 'Why did you do such and such?'"

Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah, the Exalted, sent down: ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾. It is a command from Allah, the Exalted, to His Prophet (ﷺ) to convey His message to his people and to all whom he was sent to. By His saying ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾ He means: "Proceed and separate," as Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"And as if they were a rababa, and as if he were a yasir who pours out upon the arrows and divides them [yaṣda'u]..." He means by His saying yaṣda': yufarriq (divides), with the arrows.

Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾, he said: "With the Qur'an."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr or another of the scholars, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they were circumambulating the House, and he stood, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood beside him. Al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib passed by him, and Jibril struck his face with a green leaf, and he became blind. Al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth passed by, and Jibril pointed at his belly, and his belly swelled with dropsy, and he died of it. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah passed by, and Jibril pointed at the trace of a wound at the bottom of his heel, which he had received two years earlier, while he was dragging his sibal (meaning his waist-wrapper). This was because he had passed by a man of Khuzaʿah who was fletching an arrow, and a shaft from his arrow caught in his wrapper and scratched his leg with that scratch, which was nothing, but it festered and killed him. Al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi passed by, and Jibril pointed at the sole of his foot. He went out on his donkey heading to al-Taʾif, and it stumbled on a shibriqah (a thistle), and a thorn entered the sole of his foot from it, and it killed him.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The shibriqah is what is known as the hasak (star thistle). From it comes ḥabana [[As written in the manuscript no. 100, Tafsir, Dar al-Kutub (folio 69 recto), and perhaps some of the phrase has dropped out. Its original form: the shibriqah: the singular of the shibraq, known as the hasak. It is said: he died of it ḥabana, and al-ḥīn... etc. See the account of God's sufficing His Prophet against the mockers in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (Halabi edition, 2: 50–52 of the first edition), for the author transmitted it here, with slight variation in some wording.]]—and the ḥabana is the yellow water (dropsy). Al-Harith ibn al-Talatilah passed by, and Jibril pointed at his head, and he discharged pus from his nose and died.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad al-Qurashi, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Their leader was al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and he was the one who gathered them.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ziyad, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, he said: The mockers were al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, Abu Zamʿah, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, and al-Harith ibn ʿAyṭalah. Jibril came to him and pointed with his finger at the head of al-Walid, and said: "You have done nothing," and he said: "He is sufficed." He pointed with his hand at the sole of al-ʿAs, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have done nothing," and he said: "He is sufficed." He pointed with his hand at the eye of Abu Zamʿah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have done nothing," and he said: "He is sufficed." He pointed with his finger at the head of al-Aswad, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Leave my maternal uncle to me." He said: "He is sufficed." He pointed with his finger at the belly of al-Harith, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have done nothing," and he said: "He is sufficed." He said: Then al-Walid passed by a smith of Khuzaʿah while he was dragging his garments, and a bur or shurrah (a spark) of iron clung to his garment, while women were before him, and he began to be shy of stepping on those who would pull it free, and it kept scratching his leg until he was ill and died. Al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il mounted a white mule of his for some need in the lower part of Makkah, and when he dismounted, he set the sole of his foot on a shibriqah, and his leg itched, and he kept scratching it until he died. Abu Zamʿah went blind, the ulcer (al-ukalah) took hold of the head of al-Aswad, and al-Harith was seized with water in his belly.

* Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, he said: They were five men of Quraysh: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, Abu Zamʿah, al-Harith ibn ʿAyṭalah, and al-Aswad ibn Qays.

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, he said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and al-Harith ibn ʿAyṭalah.

* Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah related to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, he said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, and al-Harith ibn ʿAyṭalah.

* Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: I said to al-Zuhri: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrimah disagreed about a man among the mockers. Saʿid said he was al-Harith ibn ʿAyṭalah, and ʿIkrimah said he was al-Harith ibn Qays. He said: Both are right; his mother was called ʿAyṭalah and his father was Qays.

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Husayn, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: The mockers were seven, and he named four of them.

* Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father related to us, from Israʾil, from Jabir, from ʿAmir: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, he said: They were five men from Quraysh: al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, who was sufficed by a headache he got, so that his brain flowed out until he spoke through his nose; al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, who was sufficed by a man of Khuzaʿah who was fixing an arrow of his, when a splinter flew off and he stepped on it and died; Hibar ibn al-Aswad; ʿAbd Yaghuth ibn Wahb; and al-Harith ibn ʿAyṭalah.

* Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Israʾil related to us, from Jabir, from ʿAmir: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, he said: All of them were from Quraysh: al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, who was sufficed by a headache that struck his head, so that his brain flowed until he could only speak from beneath his nose; al-Harith ibn ʿAyṭalah, with a worm in his belly; the son of al-Aswad, who was sufficed by smallpox; al-Walid, who was sufficed by a man going to fix an arrow of his, when a splinter fell and he stepped on it; and ʿAbd Yaghuth, who was sufficed by blindness, which took his sight.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, and from Miqsam, regarding ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, he said: They were al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, ʿAdiy ibn Qays, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib. They passed by the Prophet (ﷺ), one by one, while Jibril was with him. When one of them passed by him, Jibril would say: "How do you find this one?" He would say: "Wretched slave of Allah." Jibril would say: "We have sufficed you against him." As for al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, he stumbled, and a shaft caught in his garment; when he went to sit down, it cut his main artery and he bled and died. As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, he was brought a branch with thorns, and it was struck against his face, so that his eyeballs ran down his face. He used to say: "Muhammad invoked a supplication against me, and I invoked one against him; my supplication was answered and his was answered. He invoked that I be blinded, and I was blinded. I invoked that he be alone and solitary among the people of Yathrib, and so it was." As for al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, he stepped on a thorn, and his flesh fell away from his bones until he died. As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and ʿAdiy ibn Qays, one of them got up at night, thirsty, and drank water from a jar, and he kept drinking until his belly burst and he died; and as for the other, a snake bit him and he died.

* Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah and ʿUthman, from Miqsam, the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Ibn Thawr.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿As We sent down upon the dividers, who made the Qur'an into parts﴾, they were a group of five men from Quraysh who divided the Qur'an, some of them claiming it was sorcery, some claiming it was poetry, and some claiming it was the fables of the ancients. As for one of them, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, he came upon the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) while he was by the House, and the angel said to him: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah, as for him being my maternal uncle..." He said: "We have sufficed you." Then al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah came upon him, and the angel said: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." Then ʿAdiy ibn Qays, brother of the Banu Sahm, came upon him, and the angel said: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." Then al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib came upon him, and the angel said to him: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." Then al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il came upon him, and the angel said to him: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, he was brought a branch of thorns and it was struck against his face until his eyeballs ran down his face, and after that he would say: "Muhammad invoked a supplication against me and I invoked another against him; Allah answered him concerning me and Allah answered me concerning him. He invoked that I be bereaved and blinded, and so it was. I invoked that he become a fugitive and an outcast, so we drove him away with the Jews of Yathrib and the thieves of the pilgrims, and so it was." As for al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, he went to put on his garment, and a stray arrow caught his garment and struck his main artery or his ankle, and he was afflicted with all of that and died. As for al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, he stepped on a thorn, and he was afflicted with it; his flesh began to fall away, limb by limb, until he died in that state. As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and ʿAdiy ibn Qays, I do not know what befell them.

It has been related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), on the day of Badr, forbade his companions from killing Abu al-Bakhtari, and said: "Take him alive, for he had a good deed." The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Abu al-Bakhtari, we have been forbidden to kill you, so come to safety and security." Abu al-Bakhtari said: "And my nephew with me?" They said: "We were only commanded regarding you." They pressed him three times, but he refused unless his nephew was with him. He then spoke harshly to the Prophet (ﷺ), so a man of the people charged at him and stabbed him and killed him. His killer came back as if a mountain were on his back, fearing that the Prophet (ﷺ) would blame him. When the Prophet (ﷺ) was informed of his words, he said: "May Allah remove him far away and destroy him." These are the mockers about whom Allah said ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, and they are the five about whom ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ was said. They mocked the Book of Allah and His Prophet (ﷺ).

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, they were from Quraysh.

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, and Ibn Abi Bazzah claimed that they were al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah al-Wahid, al-Harith ibn ʿAdiy ibn Sahm ibn al-ʿAyṭalah, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Qusayy, who is Abu Zamʿah, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, who was the maternal cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: ʿAmr ibn Dinar informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, similar to the report of Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Muhammad ibn Thawr, except that he said: They were eight. Then he counted them and said: All of them died before Badr.

* * *

As for His words ﴿who set up with Allah another god. But they are going to know﴾:

This is a threat from Allah, the Exalted, and a warning to the mockers, whom He informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that He had sufficed him against, by His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, We have sufficed you, O Muhammad, against those who scoff at you, who set up a partner with Allah in His worship. So they are going to know what punishment of Allah they will meet when they return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and what calamity will descend upon them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 15, verses 95–96:

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers (95) who set up with Allah another god. But they are going to know (96)﴾

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers, O Muhammad, those who ridicule you and scoff at you. So proclaim openly what you are commanded, and fear nothing but Allah, for Allah is sufficient for you against whoever opposes you and harms you, just as He sufficed you against the mockers." The chiefs of the mockers were a known group of men from Quraysh.

Mention of their names: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad related to me, saying: The greatest of the mockers were

as follows:

I invoked that he be alone and solitary among the people of Yathrib, and so it was." As for al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, he stepped on a thorn, and his flesh fell away from his bones until he died. As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and ʿAdiy ibn Qays, one of them got up at night, thirsty, and drank water from a jar, and he kept drinking until his belly burst and he died; and as for the other, a snake bit him and he died.

* Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah and ʿUthman, from Miqsam, the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Ibn Thawr.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿As We sent down upon the dividers, who made the Qur'an into parts﴾, they were a group of five men from Quraysh who divided the Qur'an, some of them claiming it was sorcery, some claiming it was poetry, and some claiming it was the fables of the ancients. As for one of them, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, he came upon the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) while he was by the House, and the angel said to him: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah, as for him being my maternal uncle..." He said: "We have sufficed you." Then al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah came upon him, and the angel said: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." Then ʿAdiy ibn Qays, brother of the Banu Sahm, came upon him, and the angel said: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." Then al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib came upon him, and the angel said to him: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." Then al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il came upon him, and the angel said to him: "How do you find this one?" He said: "Wretched slave of Allah," and he said: "We have sufficed you." As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, he was brought a branch of thorns and it was struck against his face until his eyeballs ran down his face, and after that he would say: "Muhammad invoked a supplication against me and I invoked another against him; Allah answered him concerning me and Allah answered me concerning him. He invoked that I be bereaved and blinded, and so it was. I invoked that he become a fugitive and an outcast, so we drove him away with the Jews of Yathrib and the thieves of the pilgrims, and so it was." As for al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, he went to put on his garment, and a stray arrow caught his garment and struck his main artery or his ankle, and he was afflicted with all of that and died. As for al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, he stepped on a thorn, and he was afflicted with it; his flesh began to fall away, limb by limb, until he died in that state. As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and ʿAdiy ibn Qays, I do not know what befell them.

It has been related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), on the day of Badr, forbade his companions from killing Abu al-Bakhtari, and said: "Take him alive, for he had a good deed." The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Abu al-Bakhtari, we have been forbidden to kill you, so come to safety and security." Abu al-Bakhtari said: "And my nephew with me?" They said: "We were only commanded regarding you." They pressed him three times, but he refused unless his nephew was with him. He then spoke harshly to the Prophet (ﷺ), so a man of the people charged at him and stabbed him and killed him. His killer came back as if a mountain were on his back, fearing that the Prophet (ﷺ) would blame him. When the Prophet (ﷺ) was informed of his words, he said: "May Allah remove him far away and destroy him." These are the mockers about whom Allah said ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, and they are the five about whom ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ was said. They mocked the Book of Allah and His Prophet (ﷺ).

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, they were from Quraysh.

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, and Ibn Abi Bazzah claimed that they were al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah al-Wahid, al-Harith ibn ʿAdiy ibn Sahm ibn al-ʿAyṭalah, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Qusayy, who is Abu Zamʿah, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, who was the maternal cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: ʿAmr ibn Dinar informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, similar to the report of Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Muhammad ibn Thawr, except that he said: They were eight. Then he counted them and said: All of them died before Badr.

* * *

As for His words ﴿who set up with Allah another god. But they are going to know﴾:

This is a threat from Allah, the Exalted, and a warning to the mockers, whom He informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that He had sufficed him against, by His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, We have sufficed you, O Muhammad, against those who scoff at you, who set up a partner with Allah in His worship. So they are going to know what punishment of Allah they will meet when they return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and what calamity will descend upon them."

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Indeed, We know that your breast becomes constricted by what they say. So glorify your Lord with praise and be among those who prostrate.﴾

God, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And We certainly know, O Muhammad, that your breast is constricted by what these polytheists of your people say, by their denial of you, their mockery of you, and of what you have brought them, and that this distresses you. ﴿So glorify your Lord with praise﴾ means: turn, in what befalls you of a matter you dislike from them, to thanking God, praising Him, and prayer. God will then suffice you against what concerns you." This is similar to the report transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that whenever a matter distressed him, he would resort to prayer.

* *

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty.﴾

God, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): "And worship your Lord until death comes to you, which is certain." It has also been said that *al-yaqin* means that which is certain, just as it is said *khamr 'atiq* (aged wine), meaning *mu'attaqa* (aged).

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id told us, from Sufyan, who said: Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, regarding ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾: "Death."

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, and al-Harith ibn ... told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us; and al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Abd Allah told us, from Warqa', all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

- Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say regarding ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾: "Death."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾: "He means death."

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada regarding ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾: "The certainty is death."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, similarly.

- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Mubarak ibn Fudala, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾: "Death."

- Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Tariq, from Salim, similarly.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾: "Death. When death comes to him, there comes to him the confirmation of what God said to him and the report of the matters of the Hereafter."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Kharija ibn Zayd ibn Thabit informed him, from Umm al-'Ala', a woman of the Ansar who had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that she informed him: "They drew lots among the Emigrants, and 'Uthman ibn Maz'un fell to us, so we housed him in our dwellings. He became ill with the illness from which he died. When he died, was washed and shrouded in his garments, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered, and I said: 'O Uthman ibn Maz'un, may God's mercy be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib. My testimony concerning you is that God has honored you.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'As for him, the certainty has come to him, and by God, I hope for good for him.'"

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd told us, saying: Ibn Shihab told us, from Kharija ibn Zayd, from Umm al-'Ala', a woman of their women, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

- Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Isma'il informed us, from Muhammad ibn Shihab, that Kharija ibn Zayd told him, from Umm al-'Ala', a woman of them, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly, except that in his report he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for him, he has witnessed the certainty."
